title: Lakin
html_source: Likely from “ladykin” (“little lady”), a term of affection used in the Elizabethan era and sometimes applied to the Virgin Mary, as in the following quotation from the Tempest (1610): “By'r lakin, I can go no further, sir; / My old bones ache…” (3.2)
